Panel Data    Definition

Panel data

Panel data(longitudinal data):
     Contains multiple entities from multiple times.
    Suppose we have k regressors, the panel data is:

                 (X1it, X2it, · · · , Xkit, Yit), i = 1, · · · , n, t = 1, · · · , T.





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                             December 9, 2024            4 / 18

Panel Data   Model and endogeneity

Model specification and endogeneity




Model specification for panel data:

                  yit = β0 + β1x1,it + · · · + βkxk,it + (αi + γt + eit)

where the composite error uit = αi + γi + eit, and αi is the individual fixed effect,
γt is the time fixed effect, eit is the idiosyncratic error and it is assumed that
E(eis|x1,it, · · · , xk,it) = 0 or at least Cov(xj,it, eis) = 0 for all j, t, s.


Endogeneous issue
      Practically, we usually perceive that Cov(xj,it, αi) ̸= 0, Cov(xj,it, γt) ̸= 0.
     Pooled OLS regression results in biased and inconsistent estimation.

Estimation Methods for Panel Data    Panel data with T=2: FD model

First-differenced estimation


Suppose we have panel data with T=2, there is only 1 explanatory variable, and
we only consider the entity fixed effects:

                               yit = β0 + β1xit + (αi + eit)

Suppose it is proved that Cov(xit, αi) ̸= 0, we can use OLS to estimate the
following model:

     (yi,t=2 −yi,t=1) = δ0 + β1(xi,t=2 −xi,t=1) + (αi −αi) + (ei,t=2 −ei,t=1)

                    ∆yi = δ0 + β1∆xi + ∆ei  (1)

Since Cov(xit, eis) = 0, we know that Cov(∆ei, ∆xi) = 0.

So, using OLS to estimate equation (1) gives a consistent estimator ˆβ1,F D

Note: ˆβ1,F D is unbiased and consistent if we assume E(eis|xit) = 0.

Estimation Methods for Panel Data    Panel data with T>2: FE model

Fixed effects estimation (demeaned OLS regression)



Consider the same model on page 7 but with T>2, we can use OLS to estimate
the following model:

    PTt=1 yit          PTt=1 xit      PTt=1 αi      PTt=1 eit(yit −           ) = δ0 + β1(xit −           ) + (αi −          ) +(eit −           )
        T                   T             T            T
                                            |      {z0      }

                                           ˜yit = δ0 + β1˜xit + ˜eit  (2)

 .
Since Cov(xit, eis) = 0, we know that Cov(˜eit, ˜xit) = 0.

So, using OLS to estimate equation (2) gives a consistent estimator of ˆβ1,F E.

ˆβ1,F E is more efficient than ˆβ1,F D when T > 2.

Estimation Methods for Panel Data    Panel data with T>2: LSDV model

Least squares dummy variable model



Consider the same model on page 7 but with T>2, we can use the LSDV model
which is equivalent to the FE model.


We can use OLS to estimate the following model with n −1 dummy variables:

                      yit = β0 + β1xit + δ2D2 + · · · + δnDn + eit

where D2, · · · , Dn are the binary variables indicating different entities.

LSDV model gives a consistent estimator ˆβ1,LSDV whose properties are the same
to the ˆβ1,F E.


This method is impractical when n is very large.

Estimation Methods for Panel Data    Estimation methods for two-way fixed effects model

Estimation strategy





We can use the following 3 ways to estimate a two-way fixed effects model
according to the previously mentioned 3 methods:
    Use OLS to estimate the model with n −1 and T −1 binary variables.

    Use OLS to estimate the ”entity and time-demeaned” model.
    Use OLS to estimate the model based on the changes in variables.(from i −1
     to i and t −1 to t)

A possible mixed method:
    Use OLS to estimate the model with T −1 binary variables based on the
     ”entity-demeaned” data.

DID Model   Setup

Settings


When choosing the DID model to estimate the effects of treatment, we can
observe the data from two groups and two time periods:

two groups
     treatment group: Di = 1
     control group: Di = 0

two time-periods:

     pre-treatment period: T = 0

     post-treatment period: T = 1


The average effect of the treatment of the treated(ATT):

                    τAT T = E[Y1i(1) −Y0i(1)|Di = 1]

The problem is that we cannot obtain E[Y0i(1)|Di = 1].




            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                             December 9, 2024           12 / 18

DID Model    Estimation strategy

Parallel trend assumption

We can obtain the following 4 types of data:





Parallel trend assumption:
    The trends in the outcome variable for both treatment and control groups
     during the pre-treatment period are the same:

              E[Y0i(1) −Y0i(0)|Di = 1] = E[Y0i(1) −Y0i(0)|Di = 0]
                    unknown| {z }

So, the average effect of the treatment of the treated(ATT):

                    τAT T = E[Y1i(1) −Y0i(1)|Di = 1]

          = {E[Y1i(1)|Di = 1] −E[Y0i(0)|Di = 1]}−

                    {E[Y0i(1)|Di = 0] −E[Y0i(0)|Di = 0]}

DID Model   DID estimation

DID estimation



We can use OLS to estimate the following model:

              yit = β0 + β1Treati + β2Postt + β3Treati × Postt + ϵit

where Treati is a binary variable and Treati = 1 if observation i belongs to the
treatment group, Postt is a binary variable and Postt = 1 if observation i belongs
to the post-treatment period.





ˆβ3 is the difference-in-differences estimator, which is an unbiased estimator of
the ATT if the parallel trend assumption is held.

Stata Commends

Stata Commends

 If you have the panel data, firstly let Stata identify the type of data:

                                   xtset entity year

Next, we tend to estimate a model only with entity-fixed effects:

                               xtreg y1 x1 x2 x3,fe

or use the LSDV model

                             reg y1 x1 x2 x3 i.entity

Then, we want to consider the two-way fixed effects:

                            xtreg y1 x1 x2 x3 i.year,fe

or use the LSDV model

                          reg y1 x1 x2 x3 i.entity i.year
